boundary_evidence: NOT FROM tu_map. tools/tu_map.py reports the arm9 `main` module as UNDER-SEGMENTED: one unit 0x20049f0..0x20707a4 with 2984 functions and 73 class labels, because the module's class address-spans interleave and cluster() unions them all. There is no tu_map boundary here and no `tubuild.py create` candidate id; every line below is hand-derived and independently checkable.

THE CLASS'S FULL CONTIGUOUS RUN IS 0x02043444..0x02043f4c, 25 functions, and it tiles that span exactly with no hole and no overlap (recomputed from config/arm9/symbols.txt). The lower bound is _ZN7fBase_cnwEj at 0x02043444; the byte before it, 0x02043443, is the last byte of func_020433b8, which carries no class label. The upper bound is 0x02043f4c, which is the first byte of func_02043f4c, likewise unlabelled. So the run is bracketed by unlabelled neighbours on both sides.

no foreign symbol inside the run: config/arm9/symbols.txt lists exactly 25 function symbols in [0x02043444,0x02043f4c) -- 23 with the _ZN7fBase_c prefix plus func_02043810 and func_02043880 -- and nothing else. Both func_* are ENCLOSED by named members (func_02043810 sits between Virtual34 and MarkForDestruction, func_02043880 between MarkForDestruction and OnPendingDestroy), so no cut can exclude either without splitting the class's own run. Both also read the ActorBase layout directly: func_02043810 follows sceneNode (+0x14) to the owner back-pointer the constructor writes at its +0x10, and func_02043880 touches aliveState (0x0e), shouldBeKilled (0x0f), the flag byte (0x13) and both ProcessingListNodes (0x28, 0x38).

the run is the class's WHOLE run, bar one nested-class outlier: grep of every config/**/symbols.txt in the image finds 25 _ZN7fBase_c* function symbols, 23 of them here and 2 elsewhere -- _ZN7fBase_c9SceneNode5ResetEv (0x0203b4ac) and _ZN7fBase_c9SceneNodeC1Ev (0x0203b4c4). Those two are the NESTED class ActorBase::SceneNode, not ActorBase, they are 0x8000 bytes away, and they sit immediately below _ZN4cstd5atan2E5Fix12IiES1_ inside the 0x0203b2xx-0x0203b4xx stretch that holds the very list primitives this run calls (func_0203b20c, func_0203b244, func_0203b27c, func_0203b3c0). They are a different TU and are deliberately NOT claimed here; see notes.

DESTRUCTOR-VARIANT ORDER CORROBORATES THE SOURCE FORM. mwcc emits an out-of-line destructor definition as the fixed group D2,D0,D1 (notes/tu-reconstruction-pilot-report.md sec 3). This class has exactly that in the ROM -- 0x02043d48 D2, 0x02043d78 D0, 0x02043dbc D1, contiguous -- so the three were emitted together from one object, which is only possible if they shared a TU. Contrast ActorDerived, whose destructor is defined INLINE in the header: its vague-linkage copies come out D1-then-D0 with no D2 (0x02013e80, 0x02013ea4). Two classes, two source forms, both readable straight off the cartridge.

KEY-FUNCTION CONSISTENCY, and it is a NEGATIVE that had to hold: ActorBase's first declared virtual is InitResources (slot 0), so any TU defining it as a real method emits _ZTV7fBase_c and collides with the gap object's copy of the ROM vtable. This TU keeps it an extern "C" free function, and the compiled object emits NO .data section at all -- no _ZTV, no _ZTI, no _ZTS. That is the check that the 23 other members can be real C++ methods in one TU without the vtable following them.

VPTR ADDEND, from the cartridge: the literal pools of all three destructor variants hold exactly 0x02099edc (0x02043d74 -> 0x02099edc, 0x02043db4 -> 0x02099edc, 0x02043de8 -> 0x02099edc), which is config's `_ZTV7fBase_c`, i.e. the SLOT ARRAY. A real C++ ~ActorBase() would store mwcc's own _ZTV7fBase_c + 8 (that symbol names the vtable OBJECT, two words of Itanium preamble earlier) and, with the vtable external because of the line above, would land eight bytes high. This is why the three variants are spelled as extern "C" free functions here and not as one method.

static-initialiser attribution: NO HELP, stated rather than skipped. build/tu_map.json gives main 23 sinits / 23 .ctor entries with sinit_vs_tu 'ok' but corroborated=false, and nothing in this run touches dynamically-initialised static storage -- the object emits no .init and no .bss. This boundary rests on the contiguity, enclosure and destructor-group lines above, not on sinit counting.
notes: Hand-assembled, not generated by `tubuild.py create`: tu_map cannot segment arm9/main (see boundary_evidence line 1), so there was no candidate id to create from. The manifest entry was still built through tubuild.build_manifest_entry so the schema is the tool's own; boundary_confidence and boundary_evidence were then replaced with hand-derived values.

LICENSED SPAN IS 0x02043444..0x02043dec, 24 of the run's 25 functions. The 25th, _ZN7fBase_cC2Ev (0x02043dec, size 0x160), belongs to this TU by every boundary test but is NOT admitted: the tree has no C++ for it. src/game/actors/fBase_c/_ZN7fBase_cC2Ev.cpp is a whole-function hand-written `asm` transcription whose own banner reads 'NONMATCHING ... does NOT count as matched', and config/arm9/delinks.txt has NO entry for it at all -- it is neither compiled nor enrolled today, which is why no gate has ever reported its absence. Admitting asm would let this TU claim a range it has not reproduced from source.

include/ActorBase.h's banner used to describe the class as 0x02043494..0x02043e04. Both ends were wrong and have been corrected to 0x02043444..0x02043f4c: the old start excluded _ZN7fBase_cnwEj (0x02043444, 0x50, the class's own operator new), and the old end, 0x02043e04, is not a function boundary at all -- it falls 0x18 bytes inside _ZN7fBase_cC2Ev (0x02043dec..0x02043f4c), cutting the constructor in half.

_ZN7fBase_c9SceneNode5ResetEv (0x0203b4ac) and _ZN7fBase_c9SceneNodeC1Ev (0x0203b4c4) are the nested class ActorBase::SceneNode and are a SEPARATE TU, 0x8000 bytes away in the list-primitive stretch this run calls into. Not claimed by this entry. They are contiguous with each other (0x0203b4ac..0x0203b4dc, 0x30 total) and bracketed by func_0203b438 below and _ZN4cstd5atan2E5Fix12IiES1_ above, so they are a defensible 2-function run of their own -- but a 2-function TU whose neighbours are an unnamed function and a cstd math routine is a weaker boundary claim than this one, and merging them into ActorBase's TU would require the linker to have placed one TU's text in two places 0x8000 apart, which it does not do.

include/decl_common.h is deliberately NOT included. It declares func_0203b27c as (int, int) and data_020a4b6c as `int` where this class's own sources pass two pointers and take the address of a list head; from one TU those are two incompatible extern "C" declarations of one name, which mwcc rejects as 'illegal function overloading'. The few lines it supplied are restated in the file's own reconciled extern "C" block, keeping the most complete observation of each.

_ZN7fBase_c21AfterCleanupResourcesEj is the one admitted member whose legacy file is NOT marked `complete` in config/arm9/delinks.txt: the ROM build does not compile it today and dsd supplies its bytes from the cartridge. It reproduces under the pin both as the legacy file and in TU context, but it was never enrolled -- 'matching' and 'enrolled' are different questions.
